title: dbdash.nvim dashboard
description: One dashboard: either a single chart (database / query / show) or several panels (panels / layout). Top-level bare fields (interval, args, layout) are dashboard-wide; the top-level database, query and show are the panels' defaults (without panels: the only panel). See :help dbdash-config.

database.description: The database of a single chart; with panels, the default of every panel that does not set its own (replaced as a whole by a panel's database; optional when every panel sets one).

query.description: The single chart's query; with panels, defaults of every panel's query (timeout, max_rows, autoescape).

show.description: The single chart's show; with panels, defaults of every panel's show (interval, show_countdown, countdown_format, args_show, refresh_hidden, style, ...), merged key by key.

interval.description: Global refresh: when it elapses every panel refreshes and the panels' own timers restart. Also the last default of show.interval (after the top-level show.interval). At least 1s.

title.description: The dashboard's title: on the header line above the charts, in notifications and :DbDashStatus, and meta.dashboard_title.

description.description: The dashboard's description: a template (the shared args; meta without panel fields; it cannot assign arguments) whose result is Markdown, shown by K / :DbDashDescribe; ⓘ in the header says there is one.

show_countdown.description: Count down to the next refresh of every panel (needs interval), right of the title.

countdown_format.description: Text of that countdown ({time} seconds, {clock} m:ss; default setup defaults.countdown_format).

args.description: Shared arguments: every panel can use them. A panel's query.args are its own (only that panel sees them) and shadow a shared argument of the same name there. On the command line name=value sets every argument of that name, <panel id>.name=value one panel's own (a local name nothing else has is plain name too).

panels.description: Charts placed left to right, wrapping into rows (see show.span).

duration.description: Seconds as a number, or a string with a unit: "500ms", "30s", "5m", "1h".

type.description: Database type; inferred from the URL scheme when omitted.

url.description:
Connection URL: <scheme>://[user[:password]@]host[:port][/database][?param=value&...]
User names and passwords are percent-decoded (write @ as %40, : as %3A).
${NAME} is replaced by the environment variable NAME ($${ for a literal ${).
Without a password in the URL: password_cmd, then
stdpath("data")/dbdash/passwords.json (see :help dbdash-passwords).

SQLite      sqlite:///absolute/path.db                (or sqlite3://)
            sqlite://relative/to/this/config.db
            sqlite:///:memory:
PostgreSQL  postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db        (or postgresql://)
            auth: cleartext, md5, SCRAM-SHA-256; ?options=-c%20search_path%3Dapp
MySQL       mysql://user:pass@host:3306/db           (or mariadb://)
            auth: mysql_native_password, caching_sha2_password
Redis       redis://[user]:pass@host:6379/0          (rediss:// = TLS)
MongoDB     mongodb://user:pass@host:27017/db?authSource=admin
            mongodb://user:pass@h1:27017,h2:27017/db?readPreference=secondaryPreferred
            mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster0.example.net/db   (SRV + TXT lookup,
            defaults to tls=verify-full; ?dns=host:port picks the name server)
            ?authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256|SCRAM-SHA-1
Cassandra   cassandra://user:pass@host:9042/keyspace?consistency=LOCAL_QUORUM
            (or cql://)
SQL Server  mssql://user:pass@host:1433/db            (or sqlserver://)
            with TLS: TLS negotiated inside TDS; &encrypt=strict for TDS 8
Lua         lua://   query.sql is Lua code returning rows (:help dbdash-lua)
HTTP        https://user:pass@api.example.com/v1?key=value   (or http://)
            query.sql describes the request (:help dbdash-http); https
            defaults to tls=verify-full; other ?parameters go to the server

Push sources: data arrives instead of being queried (:help dbdash-push)
Lua stream  luastream://   query.sql is Lua whose print() / io.write() output is
            the data (:help dbdash-luastream)
Script      exec://        query.sql is a script; its output is the data
            (:help dbdash-exec)
Webhook     webhook://127.0.0.1:8765/path   an HTTP endpoint; query.sql is an
            OpenAPI document (:help dbdash-webhook)

Common parameters:
  tls=disable|require|pin|verify-ca|verify-full   (default disable)
  fingerprint=sha256:AB:CD:...                    (required for tls=pin)
  ca=path/to/ca.pem                              (verify-*: trusted CAs instead of
                                                  the system store; relative to
                                                  this config file)
  tls_host=name                                  (name to verify instead of host)
  connect_timeout=10s   timeout=30s              (defaults: setup)
  application_name=dbdash.nvim

password_cmd.description: Command printing the password (first line), used when the URL has none. A string runs through sh -c (cmd /c on Windows); a list runs directly. It runs in Neovim's current directory.

lib_path.description: SQLite: path of the libsqlite3 library to load.

create.description: SQLite: create the file when it does not exist (default false).

delimiter.description: Push sources: what separates items in the output or a streamed request body (default "\n"; a "\r" before it is dropped).

cwd.description: exec:// and luastream://: the working directory (default: this config file's directory; relative to it).

interpreter.description: exec://: the program running the script, the script being its last argument (default ["sh", "-c"], ["cmd.exe", "/d", "/s", "/c"] on Windows).

capture.description: exec://: which output is the data (default stdout); each item knows its stream.

ok_codes.description: exec://: exit codes that end normally (default [0]); others fail with the end of stderr.

env.description: exec://: environment variables added to Neovim's.

stdin.description: exec://: text written to the script's stdin (then closed).

tokens.description: webhook://: the credentials of the OpenAPI document's security schemes, by scheme name: a token (http bearer, apiKey), "user:password" (http basic), or a list of them. Use ${NAME} to read them from the environment.

stream_types.description: webhook://: more media types whose bodies are cut into items at the delimiter.

max_body.description: webhook://: the largest request body (default "10MB"; larger ones get 413).

max_connections.description: webhook://: connections at the same time (default 16; more are closed).

timeout.description: webhook://: time to send the headers and each part of the body (default 10s; then 408).

allowed_origins.description: webhook://: Origin values accepted (browsers send one; default none). Requests without an Origin are accepted.

allowed_hosts.description: webhook://: more Host names accepted besides the listening address and localhost.

name.description: Argument name, used as args.<name> in templates and Lua code.

type.description: How command-line / prompt input is parsed: list "a,b,c", map "k:v,k2:v2", boolean true/false/1/0/yes/no. Escape , and : with a backslash or quotes.

default.description: Value when nothing else sets it (an argument without a value is none).

required.description: Ask for a value at start when it has none.

show.description: Include the argument in show.args_show lines (when args_show is true).

query.description: The query; sql is required except for http(s):// (an empty request GETs the URL) and webhook:// (empty: POST or PUT of anything).

sql.description:
Query template (Jinja2, see :help dbdash-templates): arguments are
{{ args.<name> }}, metadata {{ meta.<name> }} (:help dbdash-meta, e.g.
run records with ids, times and results: meta.run (meta.run.kind: "refresh" or
"callback"; meta.run.depth: 0 in a refresh, n in a callback), meta.runs,
meta.prev, meta.prev_ok (the last successful refresh, its rows in
meta.prev_ok.result): :help dbdash-runs), and
{% set args.<name> = value %} sets an argument (:help dbdash-assign-args). Lua
runs in {% lua %} ... {% endlua %} blocks and in modules imported with
{% import 'x.lua' as h %} (:help dbdash-template-lua), with args, meta, store and
the dbdash.* helpers (dbdash.run(args): this query again with other arguments);
a config with Lua is trusted once, with the files it imports (:help dbdash-lua).
Its language depends on the database:
  SQL databases  SQL (T-SQL for SQL Server, CQL for Cassandra)
  Redis          one command, e.g. HGETALL "user:1001"
  MongoDB        a JSON document:
                 {"collection": "orders", "operation": "find",
                  "filter": {...}, "projection": {...}, "sort": {...},
                  "limit": 100, "flatten": 1}
                 operation: find | aggregate (pipeline) | count |
                 distinct (field) | command (command)
  lua://         Lua code returning rows (see "Result format" at the top
                 of this file, :help dbdash-result), or a value that
                 query.transform turns into rows; it sees args, meta,
                 store and dbdash.system/query/sleep/run (:help
                 dbdash-lua)
  luastream://   Lua code whose print() / io.write() output is cut into
                 items (dbdash.emit(value) passes one as it is)
  exec://        a script run by database.options.interpreter
  webhook://     an OpenAPI 3.1 document (YAML or JSON) describing the
                 requests it accepts (empty: POST or PUT of anything)
  http(s)://     a JSON request description (empty: GET the URL):
                 {"method": "POST", "path": "/search", "query": {...},
                  "headers": {...}, "cookies": "a=1; b=2" | "cookies.txt",
                  "body": {...} | "text", "form": {...}, "redirects": 5}
                 JSON responses are decoded, other bodies stay text; the
                 result must be rows ("Result format", :help
                 dbdash-result): a JSON list of objects or {"columns",
                 "rows"} shows directly, anything else needs
                 query.transform (:help dbdash-http)

transform.description:
Lua code that reshapes the result of any database before it is shown (after the
same template as query.sql - args, meta, {% lua %}, .lua imports - without
autoescape; :help dbdash-transform). Every query goes:
query -> transform -> rows check. It gets
  rs        SQL and other databases: { columns (names), types, rows (nil for
            NULL) }; lua://: the script's value; http(s)://: the decoded body;
            push sources: one item (text, or what dbdash.emit() or a request
            gave; :help dbdash-push)
  response  http(s)://: { status, reason, headers, body, url }
  stream    exec://: "stdout" or "stderr", the stream the item came from
  params    webhook://: { path, query, header, cookie }, converted
  request   webhook://: { method, path, operation_id, content_type, headers }
  args      the arguments, meta the metadata, store the panel's table kept while
            the dashboard runs, and the dbdash.* helpers (dbdash.run(args)
            runs this panel's query again with other arguments)
and returns rows (see "Result format" at the top of this file, :help
dbdash-result). Configs with Lua ask for trust first (:help dbdash-lua).

args.description: This chart's own arguments (only its templates see them); one with the name of a shared (top-level) argument shadows it here.

autoescape.description: Render {{ x }} as SQL literals of the database's dialect (| safe opts out).

max_rows.description: Rows read at most (default 10000, setup defaults.max_rows).

timeout.description: Query timeout (default the URL's timeout, else 30s from setup defaults.timeout).

panel.description: One chart; query is required except for http(s):// (a GET of the URL) and webhook://.

id.description: Name of the panel for its local arguments on the command line (<id>.name=value); default its number (1, 2, ...).

database.description: This panel's database; default the top-level database (replaced as a whole). A panel needs one of the two.

color.description: Hex ("#3498db"), a color name ("blue", "bright_blue"), a style ("bold blue on black"), or an existing highlight group ("DiagnosticOk").

description.description: This chart's description: a template (args, meta, as its query sees them; it cannot assign arguments) whose result is Markdown, shown by K / :DbDashDescribe; ⓘ after the panel's title (in a one-chart dashboard: in the header) says there is one. With panels, it belongs in each panel.

interval.description: Refresh interval of this chart (default the top-level show.interval, then the top-level interval, else 30s from setup defaults.interval). At least 1s.

show_countdown.description: This chart's own countdown to its next refresh.

refresh_hidden.description: Keep refreshing this chart while the dashboard is not visible (paused, see dashboard.pause_hidden in setup): thresholds and errors still notify.

countdown_format.description: {time} is replaced by the seconds left, {clock} by m:ss (default: setup defaults.countdown_format).

renderer.description:
Style for the chart type (the first one is the default):
  table: box          line: canvas, asciichart     scatter/area/bubble: canvas
  bar: horizontal, vertical    histogram: horizontal, vertical
  boxplot: boxdraw    heatmap: halfblock, block    pie: bar, circle
  stat: big           text: plain
Custom styles registered with setup({ register = ... }) are accepted too.

canvas.description: Pixel canvas for canvas styles: braille (default), quadrant, block, halfblock, ascii.

palette.description: Series colors: theme (default, follows the colorscheme) or tableau.

args_show.description: Show argument values above this chart: true for the arguments its query reads (and its own query.args; not those with show: false), or a list of names.

style.description:
Chart options:
  table      border, header_style, border_style, title_style, show_lines, null_text,
             wrap (true: long cells wrap at spaces; "char": anywhere; false: one
             line cut with "…"), cell_width / cell_height (every column's width
             and most lines per cell; a cell still too long ends with "…")
  area       stacked
  bar        color, show_values
  histogram  color, show_values
  boxplot    show_outliers, show_means
  heatmap    show_values (block renderer)
  pie        show_labels, show_values, show_percentages
  text       separator (" "), null_text (""), wrap (true: at spaces; "char":
             anywhere; false cuts long lines), title_style

colors.description: Series / slice colors, by position (list) or by category name (mapping).

value_column.description: histogram, boxplot, heatmap, pie; stat: the value (default the first numeric column).

format.description: stat: Python format of the value, e.g. "{:,}", "{:.1f}", "{:.1%}".

unit.description: stat: text shown after the value.

delta.description: stat: show the change since the previous refresh.

thresholds.description: stat: color the value by thresholds; notify: true notifies when the value rises to a step.

thresholds_below.description: Thresholds apply at or below their value (lower is worse).

column_list.description: Table (and text) columns to show, in order (all columns when omitted).

height.description: Most lines a cell takes; longer ends with …

thresholds.description: Color the cells of this column by value (notify works as for stat).
Steps from least to most severe; a value at or above a step's value (at or below with thresholds_below) reaches it and the most severe step reached wins.

notify.description: vim.notify once when the value rises to this step.
